For the record, the conclusion we agreed on together with [~accountid:5fc110f647ac91006fc4977a] [~accountid:5f0ea3c39d9a1200294cef2c] [~accountid:5eda5d0647291b0b8608735a] [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] was as follows:
*_Though it’s not asked by the tax authorities we should not allow the payout receivers to differ from the invoice issuers._* _The setup where the payout receiver differs from the invoice issuer is strongly not recommended due to the the following reasons:_

* _We might be facilitating money laundering if the payout is not made to the invoice issuer. Banks can ask for additional documentation regarding the payments facilitated by us; failing to provide sufficient evidence (agreement) can lead to suspension of services._
* _We might incur problems with the tax authorities who will be unable to properly levy taxes on the relevant income of the drivers/fleets. Bolt may be held responsible for aiding and abetting or even orchestrating a tax fraud._
* _Our Driver T&Cs state that we are making the payouts to the contractual party. If we are making the payouts to any other person / entity, it should be clearly agreed via a separate agreement._
* _To reflect objectively information from the accounting perspective we should not be making payouts to non service providers in order for the balance to be correct._
* _We currently don’t have a financial license to remit money. Therefore, we are currently remitting money under a specific exemption that allows us to remit money without a license. The exemption we use applies only if we are remitting money on behalf of just one payer or payee (not both). If an invoice is issued by one player and the payout is made to another player, then we are not remitting money on behalf of one player._

Thanks a lot everyone!

Results:

* No {{userId}} in traits:
I found out that we have never used {{userId}} as a trait. Apparently, the previous setup (event BE ↔︎ Segment or Segment ↔︎ CleverTap) was responsible for this. Current implementation with RuddeStack doesn’t do this.
Anton confirmed that we can ignore it as long as we have {{partner_uuid}} — it can be used as an *id* for propagating to InfoBib and other systems.
* Registration identify event overwrites the Driver’s one:
This is not a race condition, as we literally send the identity for Registration after we create a new Driver and send the identity for it. So, my first guess won’t work — we can’t use identifySync to guarantee the order, but I checked and found out that we can ignore sending {{accepted}} status for Registrations. It should be safe, as we don’t add any new information (except *id*)
We have three options:
** Don’t send identify event at all (*Admin* changes) ⬅️ 
** Don’t set the status for this case, so that it won’t be overwritten (*Server* changes)
** Use different property name for driver profiles (that requires BE changes and a lot of work from the LCM team, so it is the worst option)

Whichever option we chose, should be agreed with LCM team.

There is a MQTT publisher which can broadcast messages to all users. Messages are then scoped to specific entity type/id and not to given admin user id: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common/blob/590e257c27e5ad1137d1d2be0bc4f9bbb098940c/src/messaging/MessagingApi.ts#L38|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common/blob/590e257c27e5ad1137d1d2be0bc4f9bbb098940c/src/messaging/MessagingApi.ts#L38] 

Unfortunately I was unable to find any implementation within Bolt server that would use this method. I am afraid some work would need to be done to enable it. I am still researching it.

A downside od this method is that we are not able to decide who will get the message, as this method allows all users to subscribe and receive messages. There are potential security implications of such approach.

{noformat}UPDATE fee
SET invoice_id = NULL
WHERE invoice_id = invoice_id;{noformat}

-- trigger invoice generation from task

{noformat}UPDATE invoice_task

WHERE id = id;{noformat}

Hey! I’ve now confirmed this with the Privacy and Legal teams and yes, we can share the fleet owner’s contact details with riders (without asking for consent).

The reason is that fleet owners are considered business entities, so their contact details are not classified as personal data and sharing them does not contradict with GDPR.

If it helps this is the newsletter sent in Norway for example: 

Email

Subject: Sharing your information with the Norwegian Tax Administration in accordance with the EU directive

Body:

Hi there,

From 2024, we are required to share your tax details, including all drivers' VAT numbers and annual income, with the Norwegian Tax Agency. This applies to income earned on the Bolt platform in 2023.
We are taking these steps as part of recent EU measures regarding data collection, verification and sharing obligations arising from Council Directive (EU) 2021/514 (the so-called DAC7).
The new process is mandatory for all taxi platforms, including the Bolt platform.
If you fail to share any of the required information with us upon request, we may be forced to suspend your account, prevent you from re-registering and withhold your payments.
We are updating our terms and conditions to accommodate these new requirements. We are also updating our privacy policy to improve transparency, and provide information about data sharing with the Norwegian Tax Agency.
If you have any questions, please contact customer support via the app or send us an email at oslo@bolt.eu
Sincerely,

The team at Bolt

This RCA (Root Cause Analysis) matches with what I would expect to happen this integration is doing. There are a few points to consider, and two ways that we can resolve this.

+The principle here, for long-term automation and P2P goals is that all Purchase Order numbers MUST be in Workday for invoices that we receive from suppliers, to drive automation and touchless invoicing. This is the long-term vision.+

# Is the *Order* number field only being used for informative purposes in Telema, therefore the OCR is working but the logic is throwing errors (as expected?).

Based on the two questions above, we can then decide which option is best here, the decision should come from Egle/Roland with input from Bolt Market team. 

# We add code logic to ONLY execute PO logic for Bolt Operations OU - but here let’s also consider scalability, and for all new launches etc, we will need to add companies logic to add complexity to the code until we get all POs into WD.

[~accountid:5f9fbc98c2e5390077ac24d6] this task can be a little bit trickier than expected… Today we use the company timezone to define the ranges we want to filter. 
This timezone is how we calculate the rides of a Month, eg: from 01/10/2020 : 00:00:00 until 31/10/2020 : 23:59:59

If we change it to start and end dates and start sending the unixtime, we will have to calculate this unix time ourselves and make sure we are using the company timezone there.
We ned to use it, because otherwise it is possible that the price we charged in the invoice will not match the rides of the CSV we export.

The following image has an example of an Admin with a different timezone and filtering by rides in October.
Since the timezones are different you can see that in the UI one of the rides is shown as if it was on 1st of November.

That said, we can find workarounds and we can make calculations with the timezones, but if we are not having a date picker in the design it could be wise to just include the {{week}} option(s) in the existing endpoint.

We can recommend adding an artificial deduplication key column to the tables. The value would be concatenated values of unique keys. It would be a string, so NULLs in the string wouldn’t be an issue. You’d also need to change the unique key reference in dbt

Some summary from my investigaton:
- endpoint timeout is 1000 ms
- it tries to read from cache (2 minute TTL)
- on cache miss, it reads from DB (performant query, but with 38% lock time) and saves in cache
- usual performance is ok, only some MAX values timeout 

1) Having is_bot stored on a less writable (thus having less locks) table can help with DB part performance
2) On cache miss, if there are many requests about same user id, there is unnecessary load generated on DB which may decrease performance (not confirmed if it is an issue here)
3) Even loop lag may take it’s part in those cases when we have a timeout (ELL is up to 300-350ms). We took some action to limit it, our current understanding makes us believe it is mainly due to current architecture of InMemoryDataStores)
4) Any infra improvements making Redis or MySQL faster can always help, but so far there is no strong reasons for upscaling them. Still some improvement is expected related to latest change in ProxySQL setup

Documentation is linked here: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CM/pages/4032921727/Process+adherence+definition+and+elements|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CM/pages/4032921727/Process+adherence+definition+and+elements|smart-link] [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CM/pages/4078043269/Issue+Tagging+Accuracy+KPI+definition|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CM/pages/4078043269/Issue+Tagging+Accuracy+KPI+definition|smart-link]

*Element definition*

The first phase included syncing with the Content team for PA and Supportability for ITA to ensure that we are in sync on what the metrics should show - it was also here that we concluded not to simply make PA a binary metric but make it composed from multiple elements.

In retrospect, a part where I was too optimistic was the investigation x solution differentiation - while it sounded reasonable in theory, we don’t really have a way to check how exactly investigation happened and hence this had to be reformulated into following what the agent wrote to the user and what actions they took instead. 

It also had to be determined whether to put escalations under this scorecard as well - this was also further elaborated with the ESC team to determine how the options should look like.

*Score and options definition*

After elements themselves were defined, their weight had to be defined and for that, it was decided that resolution comes first and foremost - hence having half of the weight - followed by the investigation and finally the bare minimum of selecting the right process and seemingly following it. All other elements are simply binary and will make the entire section 0.

It was also here that we had to decide what exact options they had and their values - this was something that was changing a lot and the learning that came from this was to make it as easy as possible - while the original options had reasoning behind them, they were a bit too nuanced and difficult to use for those using the scorecard. The values for them were then defined based on how the correctness of them was perceived and mainly how much impact it could potentially have on the customer.

*Implementation into scorecard*

This part was actually quite smooth - most importantly, we had to determine what the weight of QA vs PA/ITA is going to be, but that wasn’t too difficult a task. Besides, some elements of QA were seemingly too PA-like and essentially if one was scored down, so was the other, hence this was smoothed out and one of the elements was removed. Other than that, there were no larger issues in including this into the scorecard.

*Testing*

During testing, we uncovered that some parts were not clear to the graders, however, we luckily concluded that this was due to a lack of training and some of the parts were not completely self-explanatory, however, it didn’t seem like there was an issue on a conceptual level - rather clarity was missing. There were also some minor suggestions for more options in certain elements or change of their description, but once again nothing that would conceptually change the way this was set up.

*Learnings for the future & possible improvements*

* It always helped when we involved the potential users - perhaps in the future if any changes are made, test users should be involved from the beginning. We would often have a lot of additional context that was not available to them and we were therefore making things unnecessarily complicated.
* Less is more - when the options would be too granular, they would just become too complicated and difficult to use, so rather it makes sense to properly think through what’s necessary (and what’s commonly happening) and what are rather edge cases that don’t need their own option.
* Context matters - it’s important to try everything out in the bigger picture, for us specifically it was how PA/ITA interact with QA and making sure there are as few clashes as possible → this leads me to the first possible improvement which is unifying this even more and perhaps having only one Confluence page for both together once everything is set in place; meaning we would have everything kind of in the same language - something to consider for Q1 improvements.
* It will definitely be necessary to have a look at the scores and weights and evaluate whether they make complete sense and how they affect the total score. 
* It probably would have been a good idea to have the scorecard as one thing together from the beginning - it didn’t really hold us back that it wasn’t, but at some point we realized that it was essentially one project that we thought would be two.

*Possible next steps and projects*

* The next steps once the scorecard is rolled out and we are calibrated with suppliers (and potentially in-house teams) is to identify the biggest issues - this will require us to first get the PA data as such, but more importantly put it to context - what are the volumes? Is it critical to deal with a given issue? Are other KPIs impacted as well?
* Then come the improvement projects - while likely they will be eventually handed over to Content, we will drive some of the first ones. This will still likely have to be done in close cooperation with content by examining whether the issue lies in the process itself, a specific markets approach to the issue or just the formulations in the process
* We will also need to set up a workflow with content to ensure that the data is well received and worked with once they take over this part of the workflow

*Conclusion*

Overall, the elements of the PA/ITA KPIs have been successfully defined, together with their scores and weights. No larger issues occurred, the only observation is that the project together with QA could have been more tied from the beginning. There are some future learnings as well as ideas to be implemented that can be used in the Q1 scorecard grooming.

On 14 Dec, there were several “Failed to navigate” errors - all of them seem to be in response to a {{@navigation/RESET}} action that we send when we respond to {{@redux-session/SESSION_LOGOUT_SUCCESS}} (the initial logout itself occurs due to getting kicked for using the same credentials on multiple devices - {{@redux-session/SESSION_UPDATE_ACCESS_TOKEN_FAILURE}}).

For some reason there are also several requests to {{/getOrdersByIdsForProviders}}:

!image-20221219-153715.png|width=956,height=729!

Note that there are no actual order ids for these requests:

!image-20221219-153734.png|width=590,height=274!

As for why we try to call this endpoint while we’re actually logged out:

!image-20221219-154928.png|width=688,height=400!

{{@network/RESET_INTERNET_DISAPPEAR_TIMESTAMP}} appears in several of these breadcrumb sets. Flaky internet connection → inappropriate {{/getOrdersByIdsForProviders}} requests while logged out.

But with that out of the way (an edge-case non-useful HTTP request we can easily prevent) - what is actually causing the error we’re concerned about?

Here we’re somewhat in the darkness. There are examples where {{DREAMING_STARTED}} is not relevant:
[https://app.bugsnag.com/bolt-6/food-delivery-provider-app/errors/62fa62cda2bf6b0009741835?filters[event.since]=all&filters[release.seen_in]=2.1.4 (1271821)&filters[user.id]=8372&event_id=63a05eef00a35d0621d60000|https://app.bugsnag.com/bolt-6/food-delivery-provider-app/errors/62fa62cda2bf6b0009741835?filters%5Bevent.since%5D=all&filters%5Brelease.seen_in%5D=2.1.4%20(1271821)&filters%5Buser.id%5D=8372&event_id=63a05eef00a35d0621d60000]

A lot of connections to connectivity issues, but nothing solid, so an experimental approach makes sense.

One example experiment (see video below):

# Log out, close app, disable internet connection.
# Relaunch app, wait until app detects infinite warm up error (“Restart the app” appears).
# Restore internet connection.
# App remains in spinner mode (as expected).
# App will try to call {{/getOrdersByIdsForProviders}}, which will fail since we’re not logged in (request is not expected).
# Navigation reset will be triggered and since we’re in infinite spinner mode, we will get a silent navigation failure error in the background (navigation has not been mounted yet).

!image-20221219-180848.png|width=292,height=73!

*But we need to keep in mind that the only way this makes sense, is if the app has entered infinite warm up mode (which can happen during restarts, if connectivity is patchy and enough requests fail).* Functionally this is expected, as navigation has not been mounted ({{isAppWarm: false}}).

In this error state, every time internet drops → returns, we get one of these errors. We can remove the impractical {{/getOrdersByIdsForProviders}} requests, so that we do not trigger nav resets due to nonsensical logouts.

*However, this does not necessarily align with the error cases Jevgeni originally linked, since there is no indication that the app is in the infinite warm-up state.*

What we do know is that {{AppEntry}} was unmounted at 11:20:24 ({{userClosesApp}}):

[https://kibana-logs.elasticsearch.boltint.net/app/discover#/doc/35ccccd0-fe91-11ec-9426-89e719726b32/.ds-logs-applog-2022.12.13-000053?id=v3DuD4UB5MkZshG0tKiL&breadcrumb=%23%2F%3F_g%3D(filters%3A\!()%2CrefreshInterval%3A(pause%3A\!t%2Cvalue%3A0)%2Ctime%3A(from%3A'2022-12-13T22%3A00%3A00.000Z'%2Cto%3A'2022-12-14T10%3A00%3A00.000Z'))%26_a%3D(columns%3A\!(app.log_message%2Cmessage_params)%2Cfilters%3A\!()%2Cindex%3A'35ccccd0-fe91-11ec-9426-89e719726b32'%2Cinterval%3Aauto%2Cquery%3A(language%3Akuery%2Cquery%3A'query.device_id%3A692a997c0753bb40%2520and%2520app.log_message%3A*')%2Csort%3A\!(\!('%40timestamp'%2Cdesc)))|https://kibana-logs.elasticsearch.boltint.net/app/discover#/doc/35ccccd0-fe91-11ec-9426-89e719726b32/.ds-logs-applog-2022.12.13-000053?id=v3DuD4UB5MkZshG0tKiL&breadcrumb=%23%2F%3F_g%3D(filters%3A!()%2CrefreshInterval%3A(pause%3A!t%2Cvalue%3A0)%2Ctime%3A(from%3A'2022-12-13T22%3A00%3A00.000Z'%2Cto%3A'2022-12-14T10%3A00%3A00.000Z'))%26_a%3D(columns%3A!(app.log_message%2Cmessage_params)%2Cfilters%3A!()%2Cindex%3A'35ccccd0-fe91-11ec-9426-89e719726b32'%2Cinterval%3Aauto%2Cquery%3A(language%3Akuery%2Cquery%3A'query.device_id%3A692a997c0753bb40%2520and%2520app.log_message%3A*')%2Csort%3A!(!('%40timestamp'%2Cdesc)))]

But the app also continues polling after {{userClosesApp}}, until the refresh token becomes invalid (provider starts using their [second device|https://kibana-logs.elasticsearch.boltint.net/app/discover#/?_g=(filters:!(),refreshInterval:(pause:!t,value:0),time:(from:'2022-12-13T22:00:00.000Z',to:'2022-12-14T10:00:00.000Z'))&_a=(columns:!(app.log_message,message_params,app.wasOfflineForSeconds,app.provider_id),filters:!(),index:'35ccccd0-fe91-11ec-9426-89e719726b32',interval:auto,query:(language:kuery,query:'query.device_id:HGAJSDLT%20and%20app.log_message:*'),sort:!(!('@timestamp',desc)))] with the same credentials):

!image-20221219-183417.png|width=938,height=410!

Either the app can be closed without stopping the polling stream, or somehow the provider reopened the app a second after we received the {{userClosesApp}} message.

*But then I decided to check what happens if we soft-kill the app - swipe up from the task menu.* {{AppEntry}} is unmounted, and {{userClosesApp}} is called. *Henceforth, as long as the app remains in the background, we will get the tryToGetNavigation error every time some epic requests navigation!*

So we can amend our experiment:

# Log in, start polling.
# Kill app from task overview (soft kill).
# Log in from other device, invalidate refresh token.
# When app’s access token expires, a logout will be triggered.
# Logout involves resetting nav → we get one of these errors.

My assumption that soft-kill does not unmount {{AppEntry}} was mistaken!

!device-2022-12-19-200544.mp4|width=368,height=720!

*TL;DR - by fixing updateOrderAfterConnectivityRestoredEpic, we may be able to remove one* +*potential*+ *error source.*

*Furthermore, we can direct our suspicion at any navigate action that can be taken while the app has been closed by soft-kill from task overview - the navigation failure error is guaranteed if the app has been closed.*

Artur explained, that we need the issues with the Preserve IP address, the packet comes with the same IP, but with a different MAC, which brings such behavior. Conclusions and thoughts: 

* I remember someone from accounting saying that the Reference Invoice MUST be in the Settlement Run - that is not true. Reference Invoice can be any invoice from any period, can be paid, unpaid or partially paid. 
* Settlement Run will not turn up as critical if all Invoice Adjustments have a Reference Invoice. I did search Workday Administrator Guide, it states that the Reference Invoice can be left blank, but I think for the purpose of successful Settlement Runs, it should always be filled in:

Hi [~accountid:62c53aac7273faf658f10f90] from legal perspective, I’m afraid we cannot accept more than the following:

* The ideal scenario is: “*Do X (number of finished orders), get Y (fixed fee)*“.
* Where an ideal scenario is not possible (or business need is very high): “*Do X in period Y get Z*”. Time period should be longer rather than shorter (i.e. daily rather than hourly - “Do X within an hour” for example is far less defensible than “Do X over the weekend”) and targets should be demonstrably achievable (based on actual data). In addition to reclassification risks, shorter time periods also increase the likelihood of accidents related to the couriers.

Otherwise, we face a risk of reclassification. 

Ride-hailing is also moving away from AR slowly. Also, right now, delivery platforms are more targeted than ride-hailing platforms regarding reclassification risk.
We can confirm there is no double charge.

*Loss from Cash-block*

I'm working on using this methodology

* checking demand in the market by looking at client cancelled/driver cancelled orders
* get driver productivity (rides/oh/gmv per hour), and multiply it by the duration of cash-blocking
* Combine the two above to get the estimated loss. The metric will be "how many extra rides/OH/GMV can we get if there are no cash-block".
* Then we can get a standard cash-block impact per GMV, and define an acceptable baseline for each market

And about debt, I think we should omit that factor from the cash-block net impact. We monitor debt differently in the expected loss from debt metric

I will show both metric, including the expected loss of debt of the cash-blocked drivers.

In essence, we say that the English will prevail in all our bi-lingual agreements [and we have English because we are a global company] - because it is possible that for some reason the two versions may end up being inconsistent on a certain point - it is therefore legally required to set out which language, in the event of there being an inconsistency, should prevail. This issue was brought up by one of the agents. Personally, I did not see any significant increases, however, received the following explanation about why the EC description should be changed:

‘uncomfortable’ itself is linked to quality issues and not safety issues (in the sense of: ‘discomfort is a quality issue and not a safety issue). Due to this, issues such as the passenger feeling uncomfortable because the driver keeps ‘looking at them’ are also taken as Driver Inappropriate Behaviour quite often even when those would not need to be. Some random compliment-based comments made by drivers/riders that wouldn’t actually fall under flirting also effectively fall under inappropriate behaviour due to this as a safety issue instead of the quality issue that those would otherwise be.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.layer_waterway(bbox geometry, zoom_level integer)
 RETURNS TABLE(geometry geometry, class text, name text, name_en text, name_de text, brunnel text, intermittent integer, tags hstore)
 LANGUAGE sql
 STABLE PARALLEL SAFE
AS $function$
SELECT geometry,
       class,
       NULLIF(name, '') AS name,
       COALESCE(NULLIF(name_en, ''), name) AS name_en,
       COALESCE(NULLIF(name_de, ''), name, name_en) AS name_de,
       waterway_brunnel(is_bridge, is_tunnel) AS brunnel,
       is_intermittent::int AS intermittent,
       tags
FROM (
         -- etldoc: waterway_z3 ->  layer_waterway:z3
         SELECT *
         FROM waterway_z3
         WHERE zoom_level = 3
         UNION ALL
         -- etldoc: waterway_z4 ->  layer_waterway:z4
         SELECT *
         FROM waterway_z4
         WHERE zoom_level = 4
         UNION ALL
         -- etldoc: waterway_z5 ->  layer_waterway:z5
         SELECT *
         FROM waterway_z5
         WHERE zoom_level = 5
         UNION ALL
         -- etldoc: waterway_z6 ->  layer_waterway:z6
         SELECT *
         FROM waterway_z6
         WHERE zoom_level = 6
         UNION ALL
         -- etldoc: waterway_z7 ->  layer_waterway:z7
         SELECT *
         FROM waterway_z7
         WHERE zoom_level = 7
         UNION ALL
         -- etldoc: waterway_z8 ->  layer_waterway:z8
         SELECT *
         FROM waterway_z8
         WHERE zoom_level = 8
         UNION ALL
         -- etldoc: waterway_z9 ->  layer_waterway:z9
         SELECT *
         FROM waterway_z9
         WHERE zoom_level = 9
         UNION ALL
         -- etldoc: waterway_z10 ->  layer_waterway:z10
         SELECT *
         FROM waterway_z10
         WHERE zoom_level = 10
         UNION ALL
         -- etldoc: waterway_z11 ->  layer_waterway:z11
         SELECT *
         FROM waterway_z11
         WHERE zoom_level = 11
         UNION ALL
         -- etldoc: waterway_z12 ->  layer_waterway:z12
         SELECT *
         FROM waterway_z12
         WHERE zoom_level = 12
         UNION ALL
         -- etldoc: waterway_z13 ->  layer_waterway:z13
         SELECT *
         FROM waterway_z13
         WHERE zoom_level = 13
         UNION ALL
         -- etldoc: waterway_z14 ->  layer_waterway:z14
         SELECT *
         FROM waterway_z14
         WHERE zoom_level >= 14
     ) AS zoom_levels
WHERE geometry && bbox;
$function$

viacheslav: About Scan QR code:

We have found difference between Android and iOS: Android allows starting a ride without camera permission, enter manually, and iOS doesn't. Considered as iOS bug.

I went to check numbers: conversion from the Unlock Screen to the Scooter Details is higher for the new users on iOS than on Android. Meaning that iOS logic seem to work better, while Android is what we initially expected.

• For new users (coming through enter phone flow) iOS has 81% conversion, Android 75% from Scanner to Vehicle details;
• For all users iOS has 89% conversion, Android 88.27% from Scanner to Vehicle details; (very minor difference).
Based on numbers even while Android behaviour is expected - iOS seem to perform better. We can try to run an experiment here and to disallow scanner usage without camera permission on Android. I'd say it should be a separate feature with expectation to increase search to ride convertion.

Due to the camera permission different Android usage of manual code entry is higher. iOS - 4.11%, Android - 5.91% of users who enter the Scanner screen. This could majorly help new users experience as issue is mostly for new users only.

@abhinav.agrawal what do you think? (compilation is in this message no need to go through the whole thread).
Hypothesis can be that manual entry introduces errors more frequently and forcing users to scanning QR code should improve conversion.

To confirm the hypothesis:
• 23% of users who input code manually see an error; 
• 12% of users who scan qr code directly see an error. 
This is stat for both platforms (it is the same for each one specifically as well). Error here is not necessary related to the scooter scanning and could happen later in the flow (hard to filter for the specific error) but difference between two funnels should be correct as the approach for error tracking is the same.
